value: **Direct Callouts & Context**: "Drawing on Illich’s idea of ‘tools for conviviality’, the paper descri bes a qualitative study with urban farming practitioners to argue that food gardens can scaffold affect-based, collaborative spaces based on social, emotional, and physical feedback offered through plant-care practices." | "Specific themes illustrating these aspects are discussed as follows: Material scaffolding through emerging affordances Respondents described how their interactions with different materials to make compost, collect biomass, grow seasonal edible plants or engage in plant care helped them expand their notions of sustainability, labour, care and community engagement." | "Cultural affordances: Scaffolding local worlds through shared intentionality and regimes of attention."
